answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may submit work to an inlet. A kernel then assigns tasks only after the bond has aged and checks whether the agent’s outputs agree with independently bonded peers; proven fraud burns the stake, while honest completion unlocks it. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up capital for each identity and risk losing it, making a large fake fleet costly rather than free to create for one voyage.
